item.title: The AI Capex Bill Comes Due (Evergreen Capital)
item.description: Two-host walk-through of Evergreen Capital's Oct 22, 2026 X post: why markets were unprepared for big-5 AI capex funding, issuance and dilution, the correction, and Evergreen's estimate of >$1.3T capex in 2027 rising to >$2.5T in 2030. Ends with our interpretation for Samsung DX devices and health. Source: https://x.com/evergreencap3/status/2113362051385139661

item.title: Hermes Gets Its Own Computer: Nous x Cua Spaces (Oct 23, 2026)
item.description: Maya and Sam on Nous Research's post that Hermes can now share a computer with your team through the Cua Spaces plugin, with context from Cua and Hermes docs, and what it means for on-device assistants and health at Samsung DX.

item.title: Consumer agents are day one of wave one (Anish Acharya)
item.description: Anish Acharya argues consumer agents are a new way to use computers, not a productivity tool, with categories wide open; replies say trust, privacy and undo decide winners. Ends with interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next.

item.title: The Three Kinds of AI ROI (Evergreen Capital)
item.description: Two-host walk-through of Evergreen Capital's Oct 20, 2026 X post: AI ROI split into model providers, customers and infrastructure; why margin is shifting to customers; four scenarios for lab economics, from multiple profitable labs to labs as public utilities. Plus our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next. Source: https://x.com/evergreencap3/status/2112613447468773623

item.title: Intuitive Surgical: the robot is the easy part (scuttleblurb)
item.description: Two-host walk-through of scuttleblurb's Oct 22, 2026 deep dive on Intuitive Surgical: razor-and-blade economics, procedure-by-procedure expansion, why robots beat laparoscopy on surgeon ease, J&J and Medtronic, remanufactured instruments, plus what it means for device and health businesses.

item.title: Technological Progress and the Meaning of Work
item.description: Soumitra Shukla and Alex Imas trace 250 years of machines threatening jobs and craft identity, from the spinning jenny and the Luddites to AlphaGo, the writers' strike and mathematicians reacting to AI in 2026. Plus our interpretation for Samsung DX and personal AI assistants. Source: https://aleximas.substack.com/p/technological-progress-and-the-meaning

item.title: Meta Q3 2026: Revenue Beat and the Muse Monetization Commentary (Funda review)
item.description: The whole Funda AI review of Meta's third quarter: the revenue beat and guidance, earnings-call Q&A on ads, WhatsApp, Business Agent, Muse, compute and financing, Funda's take and model update, with special focus on management's commentary on monetizing Muse sooner. Plus our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next. Source: Funda AI report.

item.title: Kevin Kelly: The Most Improbable Agent of You
item.description: Kevin Kelly argues AI is as centralized as it will ever be, that cost per capability halves every six to seven months so today's leading model could run on a device you own within a few years, and that we want the 'only AI', a personal exoself, not the best AI. Plus our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next. Source: https://kevinkelly.substack.com/p/most-improbable-agent-of-you

item.title: The Current State of AI: Social Capital's Deep Dive
item.description: Social Capital's deck on the state of AI: the chatbot race, reasoning models, the business of AI, agentic systems, multimodal and voice, and U.S.-China primacy, plus our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next. Source: Social Capital, The Current State of Artificial Intelligence.

item.title: The AI Stack: From Minerals to the Device in Your Hand
item.description: Social Capital's AI Stack deep dive, layer by layer from energy and chips to models and applications, plus our interpretation for Samsung DX and on-device AI. Source: Social Capital, The AI Stack: A Blueprint for Technological Supremacy.

item.title: The Five Layers of AI Agents: Social Capital's Primer
item.description: Social Capital's AI agents primer: intelligence, action, governance, orchestration and economics, plus our interpretation for Samsung's personal assistant work. Source: Social Capital, A Primer on AI Agents.

item.title: Trading AI Compute: The Next Trillion-Dollar Market?
item.description: Social Capital's deep dive on financializing AI compute and whether it becomes a tradable market, with Chamath's note, plus our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next. Source: Social Capital, Trading AI Compute.

item.title: Topol: The anatomy of a personal health agent (Nature)
item.description: Two-host pod on Google Research's three-agent personal health agent in Nature, flagged by Eric Topol: results, caveats (no outcome data, 205 s per reply, 2% moderate-to-severe harm in summaries), and our view on Galaxy Watch, Samsung Health and investable gaps.

item.title: The Retention Problem for Personal Agents: signüll's Third Space
item.description: signüll argues personal AI agents sit in a weird third space: not fun enough to be entertainment like TikTok or games, not reliable enough to be infrastructure like email or banking, and one failure often loses the user. Why focused vertical agents may win, the pushback, and our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next. Source: https://x.com/signulll/status/2112571447944097822

item.title: Agent Networks: Grous on the Next Step After Personal Agents
item.description: Nick Grous (ARK) predicts agent networks, your agent working things out with other people's agents, will dominate the conversation within six months. His three-stage graphic (chatbot, personal agent, agent networks), the gaps it skips, and our interpretation for Samsung DX. Source: https://x.com/GrousARK/status/2113018408769908888

item.title: SpaceX Q3 2026: Broad Beat and a $33-37B Q1 Compute Guide (Funda review)
item.description: The whole Funda AI review of SpaceX's third quarter: the broad beat, the $33-37B Q1 2027 compute revenue guide, estimate changes and SOTP valuation, the SI, Connectivity and Space segments, financials, capex and funding, and Funda's key risks, plus our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next. Source: Funda AI report.

item.title: What Goes Quant Next? Granade on AI and the Next Quant Industries
item.description: Matthew Granade (Faint Signals) argues AI sets up the next wave of industries "going quant," after finance, political campaigns and baseball, and bets on trial law, entertainment and general management. His argument, the pushback, and our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next. Source: https://x.com/matthewgranade/status/2112966084064129429

item.title: The GPU Revenue Ladder: Tunguz on Inference Economics
item.description: Tomasz Tunguz prices one GPU card-hour four ways, from DeepSeek's theoretical $38 to SpaceX's realized $2.44, and argues large-scale inference is a healthy business. His caveats, the counterforces (token deflation, on-device inference), and our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next. Source: https://x.com/ttunguz/status/2112950420402479268

item.title: Flapping Airplanes' Billion-Dollar Bet on GPU Primitives
item.description: The Spector brothers' data-efficiency lab raises a $1B Series A (Index, Lux) on a megakernel framework that it says makes GPUs cheaper and more expressive. What they claim, what's unverified, and our interpretation for on-device AI and Samsung Next. Source: https://x.com/flappyairplanes/status/2112955212612919318

item.title: The AI World Is Splitting in Two: Waldman on Local vs Frontier
item.description: M. Waldman (Loci) argues most consumer AI requests can run locally while frontier models stay in data centers, and that the winner will be whoever routes each request. Pushback on his numbers, plus our interpretation for Samsung's on-device vs cloud vs partner split. Source: https://x.com/i/status/2112944003121324232

item.title: Nvidia's Demand in Thirds: Jensen Huang on BG2
item.description: Jensen Huang tells Brad Gerstner AI demand is far broader than two labs, and the 2027 limit is land, power and shell; pushback, plus our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next.

item.title: Thompson: Muse Spark Open, Meta + Apple, Thin and Thick
item.description: Ben Thompson (Stratechery) on Meta's open-weight Muse Spark Open running locally on Macs with Apple's help, his branch-prediction idea for free local tokens, and why cloud still wins on cost. Ends with our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next. Source: https://stratechery.com/2026/muse-spark-open-meta-apple-thin-and-thick/

item.title: Energy as Money: Brivael on Elon's Kilowatt-Hour Standard
item.description: Brivael Le Pogam argues fiat dies and energy becomes the unit of account in an AI economy; pushback from replies, plus our interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next.

item.title: Levie: Autonomous agents are the new AI form factor (Oct 20)
item.description: Two-host pod on Aaron Levie's X post about domain-specific autonomous agents, with a Samsung DX interpretation.

item.title: Parker Conrad: Token Gross Margins Are the Metric
item.description: Rippling's Parker Conrad pushes back on Vanta's Christina Cacioppo eating token costs: if intelligence isn't worth 4X inside your product, you're just reselling the labs. Plus what it means for Samsung DX and Samsung Next (our interpretation).

item.title: Ian Buck: Why Nvidia's GPUs Keep Winning
item.description: Nvidia's Ian Buck tells Tae Kim why GPUs beat custom chips (productivity, fungibility, durability), how agents make memory, CPUs and storage matter, and how power-aware software fits 30% more GPUs into data centers. Ends with our interpretation for Samsung.

item.title: Do You Trust Apple? HomeView, Home Collection and the Siri bet
item.description: Ben Thompson (Stratechery) on Apple HomeView and the LG/Schneider-built Home Collection: reliability and privacy are Apple's pitch, Siri lock-in is the risk. Ends with the hosts' interpretation for Samsung DX and Samsung Next. Source: https://stratechery.com/2026/do-you-trust-apple/

item.title: John Arnold: Why Rate Hikes May Not Tame This Inflation
item.description: Two-host pod on John Arnold's Oct 13 X post arguing fed funds hikes do little against inflation driven by AI investment and inelastic energy demand, and may backfire. Plus pushback and what it means for Samsung.
